extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare payment analysts, hospital finance staff, and stakeholders preparing comments on CMS's FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria for calculating FY2027 inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) capital and LTCH payment rates, adjustments, and related indices; used by CMS to set rates and by hospitals and stakeholders to assess impacts and submit comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forecast error adjustment threshold for CIPI
rubrics_metrics.description: Make an adjustment for forecast error only if the difference between actual increase and projected increase of the capital input price index (CIPI) for any year is greater than 0.25 percentage point in absolute terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a 2-year lag between the forecast and availability of data to measure forecast error. Forecast error = actual CIPI increase less forecasted CIPI increase. Example: a 0.3 percentage point forecast error for FY2025 (actual 2.9% vs forecast 2.6%) exceeds the 0.25 threshold, so an adjustment is proposed for FY2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity adjustment methodology (capital update framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate an adjustment for changes in intensity using a Medicare-specific intensity measure based on a 5-year adjusted average of cost per discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case-mix constant intensity = change in total cost per discharge adjusted for price level changes (CPI for hospital services) and changes in real case-mix. Absent reliable decomposition, assume one-half of annual change is due to ineffective practice patterns and one-half due to quality-enhancing technologies/complexity; therefore add one-half of the estimated annual increase in intensity to the input price index. If estimated intensity declines over the 5-year period, apply a zero (not a negative) intensity adjustment (example: zero-intensity adjustment proposed for FY2027 based on FY2020–FY2024 decline). Full methodology described in FY2011 final rule reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of forecast data for CIPI and allowance for newer data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use IHS Global Inc.'s fourth quarter 2025 forecast to forecast the 2023-based CIPI for FY2027 (projected increase 2.8%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forecast components given (vintage-weighted depreciation prices 3.3%, interest expense 0.5%, other capital expense 3.0%). CMS proposes to use more recent data if appropriate (e.g., a newer estimate of the CIPI) when finalizing the FY2027 capital update factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlier payment adjustment factor (capital)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce the standard Federal capital rate by an adjustment factor equal to the estimated proportion of capital-related outlier payments to total inpatient capital-related PPS payments (§412.308(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A unified outlier methodology uses a shared threshold across operating and capital costs (§412.312(c)); the operating outlier threshold is set so operating outlier payments are projected to be 5.1% of operating IPPS DRG payments. For FY2027 CMS incorporated estimated operating outlier reconciliation amounts into the threshold model. Example computation: estimated capital outlier payments of 3.58% produce an outlier adjustment factor of 0.9642. Outlier reduction factors are not permanently built into capital rates and are not applied cumulatively; changes from prior year shown as ratio (e.g., 0.9642/0.9616).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality requirement for DRG and GAF changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the capital Federal rate so aggregate payments for the fiscal year, after changes from annual DRG reclassification/recalibration and changes in the Geographic Adjustment Factors (GAF), equal aggregate payments that would have been made without such changes (§412.308(c)(4)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses a multi-step methodology (described below) to compute budget neutrality adjustment factors that are applied to the capital Federal rate to offset effects of DRG reclassification/recalibration and GAF changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step GAF budget neutrality methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute GAF budget neutrality in two steps: (1) a factor to ensure budget neutrality for changes to GAFs due to updates to wage data, wage index reclassifications/redesignations, and rural floor application; (2) a factor to ensure budget neutrality for changes to GAFs due to the 5-percent cap on wage index decreases policy and the transitional exception for discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first-step GAF budget neutrality factors (for wage data updates, reclassifications, rural floor) are built permanently into the capital Federal rate and applied cumulatively. The second-step (cap/transition) factor is not permanently built into the capital Federal rate because prior-year cap/transition factors are not used in current-year calculations; CMS removed the FY2026 cap/transition factor (dividing by 0.9989) before computing FY2027 factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5-percent cap on wage index decreases policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit any decrease to a hospital's wage index to no more than 5 percent from its prior fiscal year's wage index (wage index not less than 95% of prior year) (42 CFR 412.64(h)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cap is applied before the transitional payment exception; the cap/transition budget neutrality factor is calculated separately and not permanently built into capital Federal rate. Policy finalized beginning FY2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional payment exception for discontinuation of low wage index hospital policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a budget-neutral transitional payment exception for hospitals significantly impacted by the discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy for FY2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For hospitals that benefited from the low wage index policy in FY2024 and whose FY2027 wage index decreases by more than 14.2625% from FY2024, continue a transition payment equal to the additional FY2027 amount the hospital would be paid if its FY2027 wage index were 85.7375% of its FY2024 wage index. The transition ends when the hospital's wage index decrease is less than 95% for each year since 2024 (expressed as 0.95^n, with n = years since FY2024). The transitional payment exception is applied after the 5-percent cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10-percent cap on MS-DRG relative weight decreases
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a permanent 10-percent cap on the reduction in an MS-DRG's relative weight in a given fiscal year (effective beginning FY2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To implement budget neutrally, CMS computes the DRG recalibration budget neutrality adjustment in two steps: first account for reclassification/recalibration prior to applying the 10% cap, then compute an additional factor for the application of the 10% cap. Example incremental factors for FY2027: pre-cap factor 0.9986, cap factor 0.9998, combined 0.9983.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of prior-year budget neutrality factors not used in current year
rubrics_metrics.description: Before calculating current-year GAF budget neutrality factors, remove from the capital Federal rate any prior-year budget neutrality factors that are not used in current-year calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CMS divided the capital Federal rate by the FY2026 budget neutrality factor of 0.9989 when computing FY2027 GAF budget neutrality factors (see FY2022 final rule discussion for policy basis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation and application of combined GAF/DRG and cap/transition adjustment factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a combined incremental GAF/DRG budget neutrality adjustment factor that accounts for MS-DRG reclassifications/recalibration (including 10% cap) and GAF changes from wage data updates, reclassifications, MGCRB geographic reclassification decisions, and rural floor application; apply a separate cap/transition factor for the 5-percent cap and transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example FY2027 proposed factors: GAF/DRG factor 1.0139 (built permanently into capital rates), cap/transition factor 0.9913 (not permanently built). These factors do not account for changes due to DSH or IME adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital Federal rate update and composition for FY2027
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish the FY2027 national capital Federal rate by applying the update factor and the applicable budget neutrality/outlier adjustment factors to the prior-year capital Federal rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed FY2027 update factor = 1.031 (3.1%). Proposed FY2027 GAF/DRG adjustment = 1.0139. Proposed cap/transition adjustment = 0.9913. Proposed outlier adjustment = 0.9642. Combining these yields proposed national capital Federal rate $545.22 (up ~4.02% vs FY2026). All values calculated with unrounded numbers; CMS provides chart showing effects of each factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-discharge payment formula (capital)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each discharge, adjusted capital Federal rate = (Standard Federal Rate) × (DRG weight) × (GAF) × (COLA for Alaska and Hawaii) × (1 + DSH Adjustment Factor + IME Adjustment Factor, if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlier payments may be added for cases exceeding the outlier threshold. The proposed FY2027 outlier fixed-loss amount = $51,679. Shared threshold under §412.312(c) applies for operating and capital outliers and the threshold model is in section II.A. of Addendum.

rubrics_metrics.name: New hospital capital payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: New hospitals are paid 85% of reasonable costs during first two years of operation unless they elect to receive payment based on 100% of the capital Federal rate; effective third year, payment is based on 100% of the capital Federal rate (§412.304(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals may elect 100% capital rate during initial two years; absent election, default 85% reasonable cost payment applies for first two years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-of-increase percentage for excluded hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments for hospitals excluded from IPPS (children's hospitals, 11 cancer hospitals, hospitals outside 50 States/DC/PR) are updated by a rate-of-increase percentage equal to the IPPS operating market basket percentage increase (2023-based).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027 CMS proposes 3.2% based on IGI's Q4 2025 forecast of the 2023-based IPPS operating market basket increase; CMS may use more recent data if appropriate. Target amount updated per §413.40(c)(3). RNHCIs and extended neoplastic disease care hospitals follow same update.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH PPS annual update and productivity adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate by the most recent estimate of the LTCH PPS market basket less the statutory productivity adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027 CMS proposes an LTCH market basket increase of 3.2% less a productivity adjustment of 0.8 percentage point = 2.4% update (apply update factor 1.024 to FY2026 LTCH rate). Per statute, LTCHs that fail to submit required LTCH QRP quality data have their annual update reduced by 2.0 percentage points (resulting in 0.4% for non-reporters). CMS additionally applies an area wage level budget neutrality factor (example 1.0025505) to ensure changes to area wage level adjustment do not change aggregate payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH area wage level adjustment and geographic classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the labor-related share of the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate by the applicable LTCH PPS wage index, computed using wage data from inpatient acute care hospitals without regard to certain reclassification provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic classifications (labor market areas) use Core Based Statistical Areas (CBSAs) as delineated by OMB (2020 standards and Bulletin No. 23-01). CMS provides wage index tables for proposed FY2027 values for urban and rural areas in the Addendum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital Input Price Index (CIPI) vintage-weighting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The CIPI is a fixed-weight price index that must reflect the vintage nature of capital by using a weighted average of past capital purchase prices up to and including the current year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capital expenses are determined by the stock of capital (current and prior acquisitions); CIPI differs from operating input price index by capturing this vintage nature. For FY2027 CMS proposes to use 2023-based IPPS operating and capital market baskets and refers to FY2026 final rule rebasing discussion for full methodology.
